scope.description: Two demand-signal leads resolved from the August 4 Buy Canadian newsletter to original Government of Canada policy and program sources; newsletter text and linked commentary are excluded from field evidence.

source.title: Buy Canadian Procurement Policy Framework
source.locator: Purpose, application, implementation policies, and exclusions
source.summary: The official framework prioritizes Canadian suppliers, content, and materials and expands small-business access across applicable federal procurements while identifying exclusions and exception pathways.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official CanadaBuys framework, policy overview, supplier questions and answers, and ministerial exceptions guide.
followUpQuestions: Should the reviewer keep this government-wide operational procurement framework separate from the broader defence-specific Build-Partner-Buy demand source?
Which future official implementation reports can support observed-results measures without relying on media calculations?
reviewWarnings: The policy is non-retroactive and contains sensitive-operation, overseas, intergovernmental, and delivery-location exclusions.
The newsletter's contract-ownership and award-share calculations are not field evidence and are not included in the candidate.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Recovered the controlling official framework and explicit exclusion boundary.
Recovered the official overview and the three implementation policy components.
Recovered supplier definitions, thresholds, strategic-sector coverage, and non-retroactivity.
Recovered the official case-by-case exception process and approval grounds.

leads.title: Buy Canadian Procurement Policy Framework
candidateRequirements: Applicable federal procurements should prioritize Canadian suppliers and Canadian content under the Contracting with Canadian Suppliers and Content Policy.
Applicable high-value procurements should prioritize Canadian steel, aluminum, and wood inputs under the Canadian Materials Policy.
Federal procurement should reduce barriers and expand participation for Canadian small and medium-sized businesses.

source.title: Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability
source.locator: Project objective, requirements, industry engagement, and next steps
source.summary: The official project page defines a rapidly deployable long-range precision-strike capability, resilient employment requirements, integration and sustainment scope, and a path from closed industry engagement toward procurement and evaluation.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official DND project page with explicit operational purpose, resilience requirements, system-of-systems scope, engagement status, and procurement next steps.
followUpQuestions: Should the reviewer preserve this specific project as a separate demand source from the broader Defence Drone Initiative marketplace?
Which future procurement notice, demonstration, or selection should refresh the project lifecycle?
reviewWarnings: The closed industry question-and-answer activity is not an open solicitation and does not establish supplier eligibility, selection, or award.
The public project page does not disclose budget, range, platform, payload, supplier, or delivery schedule.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Recovered the official project scope, requirements, engagement status, and lifecycle next steps.
Confirmed the earlier broad initiative mentioned deep precision strike as one of six areas without an acquisition decision.
Recovered official industrial-policy context without using it to infer a project award, budget, or supplier.

leads.title: Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability
candidateRequirements: The Canadian Armed Forces need a rapidly deployable long-range precision-strike capability for deterrence, response, and joint or allied operations.
The capability must remain secure, scalable, resilient, and effective amid electronic warfare, cyber threats, GPS disruption, and air defences.
The project must integrate equipment, training, logistics, command-and-control and network interfaces, and a reliable inventory into an operational capability.
